reason: E2 directly demonstrates phase-selective recrystallization (PSR) in an FCC/B2 eutectic HEA, achieving ~35% uniform elongation and ~2 GPa true stress, which supports the core premises of selective recrystallization, reduced boundary weakness, and improved ductility with high strength. E1 concerns a different alloy system and processing route (TRIP-HEA with grain refinement) and does not directly support the specific premises about eutectic lamellar microstructures or phase-selective annealing.
premises: Selective recrystallization of the ductile FCC phase is achievable while preserving the hard phase in a eutectic HEA.
Recrystallization of the FCC phase reduces dislocation pile-ups at interphase boundaries.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups mitigates stress concentrations and delays microcracking.
The hard phase continues to provide strength after the treatment.
The treatment improves room-temperature tensile ductility while retaining or slightly increasing strength.
